name: Aleksandr Konotopskyi
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: endeavor.org/entrepreneurs (Ukraine filter, fetched 2026-08-22) lists "Aleksandr Konotopskyi" with Ajax Systems -- "designs and manufactures security systems" -- Selected: 2025, Endeavor Ukraine. || SERIAL-FOUNDER CHECK, MATERIAL AND FLAGGED: Konotopskyi ran an EARLIER venture. With school friend Yevhen Humeniuk he traded Chinese micro-earphones while working a year as a radio-planning engineer at MTS-Ukraine, then the pair built an online store for Chinese security equipment putting in $5,000 each (he was 22), and at the end of 2008 structured it as the distributor Secur; he handed Secur's management to his partner in 2014 (https://forbes.ua/company/nestrimniy-konotopskiy-velika-viyna-ne-zmogla-zagalmuvati-zasnovnika-ajax-systems-velika-istoriya-vid-forbes-08112022-9544). uk.wikipedia states Secur became "one of the largest sellers of security equipment in Ukraine" by 2012. NO revenue, turnover or profit figure for Secur exists in any source found (the 2022 Forbes Ukraine long profile, uk.wikipedia, abiznes.com.ua, fraza.ua, ajax.systems/founder-story); the only quantitative traces are the $5,000-each founding capital and the $50,000 of Secur profits Konotopskyi put into Ajax in 2011. The 2012 nominal rev10 bar is $7,131,511. There is no positive evidence Secur ever crossed it and no basis on which such a crossing could be dated or bounded, so the hit entity is Ajax Systems -- but this call rests on absence of evidence about Secur, not on a figure showing Secur stayed below, and is flagged for re-check. || BOUNDED rev10 2015-2018, both ends sourced; Ajax does not publish financials ("Ajax не розкриває фінансових показників", Forbes Ukraine, 12 Jan 2023, https://forbes.ua/news/ajax-systems-zbilshila-dokhid-na-tretinu-a-potuzhnosti-vdvichi-v-2022-rotsi-12012023-11031), so no exact year is pinnable. UPPER END 2018: the same Forbes Ukraine piece reports several investment analysts putting Ajax's 2022 revenue at $150-200M and quotes Oleksandr Matsiuk (Head of Growth, SocialTech) that "since 2018 the company has grown roughly 10x", which places 2018 revenue at about $15-20M against a 2018 nominal bar of $7,799,735 -- 92% to 156% above the bar, margin well over 20% at the low end. LOWER END 2015: in June 2015 Ajax raised $1M from SMRK on SMRK's stated principle of taking no more than 20%, implying a whole-company valuation of about $5M or less, and Konotopskyi told the Big Money interview (quoted by Forbes Ukraine) that "over the next three years revenue grew 30-fold" -- 2015 revenue is therefore about one-thirtieth of 2018's, roughly $0.5-0.7M, against a 2015 bar of $7,362,080. The 30x claim alone forces 2015 below the bar: 30x the 2015 bar would be $221M, and Ajax's revenue was still only $150-200M in 2022. The crossing is most likely 2017 but is not pinnable, so the bound is recorded as given. NOTE ON EVIDENCE QUALITY: the upper end is an analyst estimate combined with a growth multiple rather than a disclosed figure -- flagged. || a1 born 7 June 1986, Kyiv (uk.wikipedia; Forbes Ukraine gives his age as 36 in a November 2022 piece, consistent). a2 2009: NTUU KPI 2004-2009, "Telecommunication systems and networks" (uk.wikipedia, abiznes.com.ua); Forbes Ukraine describes Konotopskyi and MacPaw's Oleksandr Kosovan as "two KPI graduates", so the credential was completed. a3 = a4 under pilot rule R1: his paid employment before founding was freelance business journalism at Vlast Deneg (2007, from his third year at KPI) and a year as a radio-planning engineer at MTS-Ukraine -- neither is security-hardware work -- so entry to the domain is his own 2008 venture; confidence low. a4 2008: the online security-equipment store, structured as Secur at end-2008. a5 hit entity Ajax Systems, registered 2011 as "Scientific-Production Enterprise Ajax" with $50,000 of Secur profits. a6 2022: Forbes Ukraine valued Ajax at $500M and named Konotopskyi Entrepreneur of the Year; analysts' revenue estimate $150-200M.

name: Luca Rossettini
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: https://endeavor.org/entrepreneurs/?_paged=4 (fetched 2026-08-22) carries the D-Orbit entry -- "D-Orbit is a satellite technology provider for the traditional and new space sectors... Outlier Company... Selected: 2016" -- with Entrepreneurs "Renato Panesi, Luca Rossettini" and Local Office "Endeavor Italy". || SERIAL-FOUNDER CHECK, MATERIAL: D-Orbit (2011) is NOT Rossettini's first venture. The A Sign in Space team biography (https://asignin.space/about/team/luca-rossettini/) records that he co-founded The Natural Step Italia in 2006 and founded two ventures in 2008 -- IRTA, a drone-tracking-technology startup, and OLA Film, a special-effects company. None of the three is in the space-hardware domain, none has any published revenue, and none is described anywhere as having reached commercial scale; The Natural Step Italia is the Italian branch of a Swedish sustainability non-profit. There is no evidence any of them approached the constant-dollar rev10 bar (2008 nominal bar $7,799,735 in 2018 terms; the 2008 bar itself is well under $10M), so the hit entity is D-Orbit. Flagged because the earlier ventures exist and are simply undocumented financially. || PINNED rev10 2023, both the below-bar and above-bar years sourced, so no bounding is needed and the IPO/acquisition fallback is not in play (D-Orbit has never listed -- its January 2022 SPAC merger with Breeze Holdings at a $1.28bn enterprise value was cancelled in August 2022). BELOW BAR 2021: the Breeze Holdings 8-K/425 press release of 27 January 2022 states "D-Orbit generated 2021 revenues of approximately $3.4 million (EUR 3 million)" against a 2021 nominal bar of $8,416,707 -- 40% of the bar (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1817640/000121390022003839/ea154405ex99-1_breeze.htm). BELOW BAR 2022: the Italian statutory accounts of D-Orbit S.p.A. (Fino Mornasco, VAT 07373150965) show 2022 fatturato of EUR 3,468,206 and valore della produzione of EUR 6,572,266 (https://topaziende.quotidiano.net/lombardia/como/fatturato-d-orbit-societa-per-azioni/). At the ECB 2022 annual average of 1.0530 USD/EUR that is $3,652,021 of revenue, or $6,920,596 even on the broader production-value measure, against a 2022 bar of $9,090,274 -- still below on either measure (76% of the bar at worst). ABOVE BAR 2023: BeBeez, citing the Leanus filing report, states "Nel 2023 la societa ha fatturato 13,5 milioni di euro, l'ebitda e stato negativo per 810 mila euro, la liquidita netta pari a 39 milioni e il patrimonio netto di 32,9 milioni" (https://bebeez.it/venture-capital/la-comasca-d-orbit-logistica-spaziale-e-trasporto-orbitale-rileva-il-100-della-barese-planetek-osservazione-della-terra/). CURRENCY CONVERSION: at the ECB 2023 annual average of 1.0813 USD/EUR, EUR 13.5M = $14,597,550 against the 2023 nominal bar of $9,464,470 -- 54% above the bar. The conversion is not load-bearing: even at parity EUR 13.5M clears the bar by 43%. CAVEAT: both the 2022 and 2023 figures are the Italian S.p.A. statutory accounts rather than group consolidated accounts; the 2021 SEC-filed group figure (EUR 3M) and the S.p.A. figures are the same order of magnitude, so the group/parent distinction does not move the crossing year, but it is noted. D-Orbit's 2024 fatturato fell back to about EUR 9.96M (fatturatoitalia.it), which does not affect the first crossing. || a1 unknown after two attempts: no source found gives Rossettini's birth date or age (it.wikipedia's Luca Rossettini is a footballer, a different person). a2 2008: PhD with honours in advanced space propulsion, Space Propulsion Lab, Politecnico di Milano (asignin.space team bio; Creative Destruction Lab mentor page and multiple space-press bios agree on the 2008 PhD). Later non-degree credentials -- a 2010 Certificate in Technology Entrepreneurship from Santa Clara University -- are not treated as the terminal credential. Earlier: MSc Aerospace Engineering 2003, MSc Strategic Leadership Towards Sustainability 2005. a3 2011 under pilot rule R1, confidence low: no employer-paid work in space hardware is documented anywhere before D-Orbit. His prior paid roles were Italian Army airborne officer (left 1998), doctoral research at the Politecnico space propulsion lab (a studentship, no employment dates published), sustainability consulting via The Natural Step Italia and the two 2008 startups outside the domain; the NASA Ames stint was an internship after 2010. Founding D-Orbit is therefore his entry to the domain. A reviewer could defensibly date a3 to the start of the PhD instead, but no start year is published. a4 2006: The Natural Step Italia, the earliest co-founded venture on record; confidence low because the source is a single team-page biography and the entity is a non-profit branch rather than a commercial company. a6 2024: the year D-Orbit closed the second tranche of a EUR 150M Series C led by Marubeni (BeBeez) and won a EUR 120M ESA contract for the RISE mission (https://alumni.polimi.it/en/2024/11/15/spazio-leuropa-punta-su-d-orbit-fondata-dallalumnus-luca-rossettini/).

name: Elad Gil
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: https://www.forbes.com/profile/elad-gil/ (fetched 2026-08-22) states "Elad Gil is ranked at No. 6 on the 2026 Midas List, his 2nd appearance" and describes him as "Founder and CEO, Gil Capital... one of the most prolific solo venture investors". || EARLIER-FIRM / SERIAL-GP CHECK, THE ONE THIS BATCH WAS WARNED ABOUT -- NEGATIVE: Gil was never a named general partner at an earlier venture firm. A SEC EDGAR full-text search of Form D filings naming "Elad Gil" returns his name only in the Cosmic family of vehicles, the first of which is Cosmic - Aleph 1, L.P. Vehicles filed before 2020 that surfaced in the same search (DIHEDRAL GROUP L.P. 2016, YEDA L.P. 2018, ASSOCIATED FUNDS SPV L.P. 2018, TRIHEDRAL GROUP L.P. 2019, Cognate Investments LP 2019) were checked individually: none names Gil as a related person. The one plausibly his -- "Elad Investments, LP - Series 1" (CIK 1778988, Form D 6 June 2019, GP entity "EG GPE, LLC", 229 Jersey Street, San Francisco, later renamed Cognate Investments) -- is a series SPV reporting total offering "Indefinite" and total amount sold $0, so it is not a fund closed above any threshold and cannot fire fund100. Before 2020 Gil invested as an individual angel (Stripe's 2010 seed among the earliest reported); an angel book is not a fund with a named GP. || PINNED fund100 2020. HIT ENTITY Cosmic - Aleph 1, L.P. Form D filed 27 March 2020 (CIK 0001807070, accession 0001807070-20-000002, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1807070/000180707020000002/primary_doc.xml) reports a joint filing by Cosmic - Aleph 1, L.P. and Cosmic - Bet 1, L.P., investment fund type "Venture Capital Fund", date of first sale 18 March 2020, total offering amount $300,000,000 and total amount sold $300,000,000 with $0 remaining, and lists exactly two related persons: the GP entity Cosmic Gimel 1, LLC and "Elad Gil". The 2020 nominal fund100 bar is $80,390,318, so $300,000,000 is 273% above the bar. The margin survives the worst-case reading: even if the $300M is split evenly across the two parallel partnerships in the joint filing, each half ($150M) is still 87% above the bar. Corroborated by Venture Capital Journal, "Entrepreneur and angel Elad Gil raises $300m", which reports the same raise from 16 investors (https://www.venturecapitaljournal.com/entrepreneur-and-angel-elad-gil-raises-300m/). Later funds -- about $620M in 2021 (Cosmic - Aleph 2) and about $1.1B in 2023 (Cosmic - Aleph 3) -- are all after this one, so 2020 is the first qualifying close. || a1 1974: the MIT authority record for his doctoral thesis gives the author as "Gil, Elad B., 1974-" (https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/169156). No press source found states his birth year, so confidence medium. a2 2001: "Thesis: Ph. D., Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Department of Biology, 2001", title "Studies of the PTEN tumor suppressor gene", same DSpace record -- a primary institutional source. Prior degrees: BS in mathematics and molecular biology, UC San Diego. a3 = a4 under pilot rule R1, confidence low: no employer-paid investing role precedes his first venture. His paid employment was McKinsey & Co., then Google (product manager, June 2004 - September 2007, started the mobile team), then VP Corporate Strategy at Twitter after the acquisition; none is an investing job. His actual entry into the investing domain was self-directed angel investing from around 2010 (Stripe seed), which is not employer-paid work and which no fetchable source dates precisely. a4 2008, confidence low: Mixer Labs, which "started out as TownMe" (TechCrunch, 23 December 2009, via the Internet Archive: http://web.archive.org/web/20100113154950/http://www.techcrunch.com:80/2009/12/23/twitter-acquires-mixer-labs/), acquired by Twitter in December 2009. DATING CAVEAT: several secondary profiles date the founding to November 2007, but those pages (golden.com, now redirecting to seedtable.com) returned 403 on re-fetch and the claim could not be re-confirmed, and the WebSearch budget for the session was exhausted before a third attempt. The hard-sourced evidence is the "Mixer Labs, Inc. 2008 Stock Plan" assumed by Twitter and registered on Twitter's Form S-8 POS (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1418091/000119312522272812/d409372ds8pos.htm) plus Internet Archive captures of mixerlabs.com from March 2008, so 2008 is recorded as the conservative sourced year; a reviewer with search access should test 2007. No venture earlier than Mixer Labs was found. a6 2023: his third fund, Cosmic - Aleph 3, took commitments of close to $1.1 billion from 54 investors (Form D/A 3 November 2023, CIK 0001922165; reported by PitchBook News, "Prominent solo VC Elad Gil raises over $1B for his third fund").
